summary: Return the unique elements that appear in both arrays.
mainInsight: Put one array into a set and iterate over the other, collecting elements that are in the set; use a set for the result to remove duplicates. Alternatives: sort both and use two pointers, or binary search.

approaches.name: Binary search
approaches.summary: Search each element of the smaller array in the sorted larger one.

commonMistakes: Assuming a sorted result is required

promptVariants: Which structure gives the unique common elements most simply?
options: Two sets: O(1) membership and duplicates disappear automatically
Two sorted lists: the first match you find is always unique
A max-heap holding both arrays merged together into one heap
A stack: push one whole array and pop elements while they match
cards.answer: Two sets: O(1) membership and duplicates disappear automatically
cards.explanation: The result must contain each element once.

incorrectOptionExplanations.A max-heap holding both arrays merged to: Heaps do not detect common elements.
incorrectOptionExplanations.A stack: push one whole array and pop el: Stacks do not provide membership tests.

promptVariants: How do you avoid duplicates in the result?
What does the two-pointer variant require?
cards.answer: Collect results into a set (or skip equal neighbours when using sorted arrays). The two-pointer variant requires both arrays to be sorted, advancing the pointer with the smaller value and recording equal values once.
cards.explanation: Intersection II keeps duplicates by counting.
Building both sets and checking membership is linear.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Space complexity (excluding the input): ___
What is the result for [3, 8, 3, 5] and [5, 3, 3, 9, 3]?
options: [3, 5] in any order: each shared value appears once
[3, 3, 5]: duplicates are kept up to the smaller count
[9]: only the value that is unique to the second array
cards.answer: [3, 5] in any order: each shared value appears once
cards.explanation: The shared values are 3 and 5, and each is reported once; the problem accepts any order.

incorrectOptionExplanations.[3, 3, 5]: duplicates are kept up to the: That is Intersection II, which keeps duplicates; this problem wants unique values.
